flags.why: “Chiến tướng” means a general who commands in battle, whereas “warlord” adds independent political power that the word does not express ([dictionary](https://loigiaihay.com/tu-dien-tv/chien-tuong-emCaHqtvJsWZy.html)).
“Chủ xị” is a colloquial expression, so the untagged gloss misleadingly presents it as a neutral term for a host ([dictionary](https://v2.rung.vn/dict/vn_vn/Ch%E1%BB%A7_quy%E1%BB%81n)).
“Chủ xị” is chiefly Southern usage and lacks its regional label ([Bình Định newspaper](https://baobinhdinh.vn/viewer.aspx?mabb=146944&macm=6&macmp=7)).
The meal or drinking-party sense of “chủ xị” is chiefly Southern usage and lacks its regional label ([Bình Định newspaper](https://baobinhdinh.vn/viewer.aspx?mabb=146944&macm=6&macmp=7)).
